title: Incremental transaction storage and indexed order nodes: validation
status: implemented and validated locally; not committed or pushed

architecture.transaction: Keep command-level isolated candidates. Persistent im roots replace whole-book/table copies; writes copy affected tree/hash-trie paths.
architecture.orders: Stable order ID handles, persistent hash index, doubly linked FIFO nodes, ordered price levels, cached total quantity, incremental account order indexes.
architecture.accounts: SharedMap now uses im::OrdMap, including balances, reservations, positions and derived margin state. Nested portfolio balances use the same mechanism.
architecture.clearing: Engine trade settlement uses the enclosing command rollback candidate. Public account settlement retains independent atomic behavior.
architecture.perpetual_reservation_index: Recover lazily once from checkpoints, then maintain per-account persistent sets incrementally instead of rebuilding after writes.
architecture.outer_candidates: Large conditional/protection tables and liquidation queues share roots; asset ledger uses existing chunk-sharing History. Exchange/room/journal commit boundaries remain.
architecture.checkpoint: Retain legacy JSON queue/map fields. Serialize FIFO queues and legacy order locations; rebuild links, quantity aggregates and account indexes on read.
architecture.decision: A project-scale change that preserves existing failure and persistence contracts. It has higher per-node matching overhead than the original mutable queues; it is not an exchange-grade arena/undo-log implementation.

correctness.differential_method: Both frozen old and current Rust crates execute the same seeded commands. Compare all returned execution/events/errors and depth; compare complete serialized state every 100 commands; import actual old checkpoints into current and continue.
correctness.differential_scope: 5 seeds, 16 accounts, limit/post-only/IOC/FOK/market/cancel/amend, duplicate/invalid IDs and quantities. Randomized stream uses Both position side and excludes reduce-only; existing core/server tests cover hedge/reduce-only/protection/liquidation.
correctness.permanent_regression: 320 commands and expected events/depth generated solely from frozen old implementation; plus indexed-node invariants, persistent candidate isolation, old checkpoint reconstruction and later-maker clearing-failure rollback tests.
earlier_failures: Missing Python on PATH caused four process-plugin test failures; corrected by repository venv PATH.

Two process-plugin tests timed out during a later parallel workspace test run concurrent with release compilation. Final single-threaded workspace and required PostgreSQL runs passed without changing any timeout threshold. Logs retained.

order_transactions.aggregation: median of 6 block medians; 2 runs x 3 blocks
order_transactions.scope: Release local microbenchmark of current dirty checkout. One funded account, no fills, empty history, no server/journal/network. Seed setup and external reset excluded; apply's internal clone and old-state drop included. 10 warmups, 80 samples, 3 blocks; ascending/descending sizes. Raw operations use an externally cloned reset: legacy queues are unshared, persistent nodes share roots with the seed. Raw add is prepared by add/cancel outside the timer (spare queue capacity in the legacy build). Account release and engine apply measured with live originals sharing account tables, as transaction candidates do. Seed book/accounts and order events checked against ordinary apply at n=16, canonicalizing unordered HashSet serialization.

matching_transactions.aggregation: median of 6 block medians; 2 runs x 3 blocks
matching_transactions.scope: Release, two spot accounts, one price, unit makers, 1/100/1000 complete fills. Empty input event history. External reset excluded; internal candidate clone and clearing included. Timed event-count validation included equally in both builds; account assertions excluded. 5 warmups, 20 samples, 3 blocks. Seed validated against ordinary apply at 16 makers. No server, journal, network or durable commit timing.

performance.reading_raw_results: Raw book operations exclude reset cloning. Legacy reset clones produce private queues; current resets share persistent roots, so their first-write detachment is timed. These figures describe book operations on candidate resets, not a pure algorithm comparison on two exclusively owned books.
performance.reproduce_baseline: Compile the identical examples against .local/transaction-refactor/baseline/exchange-core using its saved standalone manifest and matched lockfile. Production source was copied before edits, including pre-existing user changes. The original pre-refactor study binary and source receipt are also retained.
limits: Synthetic spot workloads: one account/no fills or two accounts/unit maker fills, 1/100 levels, empty input event history.
No measured end-to-end server/actor/room/durable journal/HTTP/WebSocket/network/queue waiting or snapshot publication improvement.
No perpetual throughput, retained long-history or many-account/many-market scale qualification.
Whole checkpoint serialization remains O(total state). History cloning retains existing chunk-root costs; price/market/config and some outer metadata still use ordinary containers.
Persistent node maintenance and path copying raise raw candidate matching overhead. Tiny concentrated books and single-fill commands may be slower; inspect all matrix rows, not just large-book wins.
No allocator/peak-memory benchmark or deployment SLA. Sub-microsecond medians are near timer resolution and should not be treated as precise speedup ratios.
